_comment: The bundled library, listed on Torchbearer's title screen. id / name / type / description are asserted against each pack's own `pack` block by test/smoke.mjs, so this file cannot drift from the JSON it describes. To add a pack: drop the .json in this folder and add an entry here. What a pack actually contains is counted from the pack itself on the load confirmation, not written down twice. Two files in this folder are not packs and are not listed: index.json, and schema.json, which is the contract every pack here is validated against.

packs.name: The Long Vigil at Thornwake Bridge
packs.description: A level 3 one-shot: two mercenary companies have refought the same five minutes on a haunted bridge for fifty years. A skill-driven investigation opens a genuine third option — end the vigil with a blade, or end it by finally being believed. Also carries The Bell and the Bridge, the two-adventure campaign that runs it after the bundled Bell of Barrowmoor.

packs.name: Embers of the Hold (Sample Expansion)
packs.description: A worked example of every pack collection: the orc ancestry, a background, shared feats, a new spell, a monster, a companion, and a two-battle mini-adventure.

packs.name: The Quarter-Day at Cold Harrow
packs.description: A level 3 one-shot about bookkeeping. Ninety years ago a lead mine drowned with sixty men in it, and the village wrote a contract with whatever answered from the water. The tithe has been paid three hundred and sixty times. Tonight's is short, and the village has decided you are the difference — unless you can read the ledger well enough to prove the debt was cleared in 1391 and nobody ever closed the account.

packs.name: A Bestiary of the Harrowmoor
packs.description: Ten monsters for levels 1 to 6, written for the wet lead country around Cold Harrow and usable anywhere. Every one of them carries the two fields Phase 3 added — reach in cells, and the reactions the engine actually implements — and every one has the lore line a critical Recall Knowledge prints, written as the thing a player could act on. No adventure, no scenes: this is stock for somebody else's encounters.
